transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-04-08
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Ravi Singh (Redwood SE); Jenna Lee (BrightCart - Head of ML); Carlos Mendez (BrightCart - Platform Eng); Priya Nair (BrightCart - PM)

Summary (auto): quick review of this week's cache telemetry; focus on prefix cache hit rate improvements and KV cache eviction experiments; plan next benchmarks and artifacts to share.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick sanity check on audio — can you hear me OK?
[00:05] Jenna (BrightCart): Yep, loud and clear.
[00:07] Carlos: good.
[00:10] Maya: Cool. Ravi — do you want to jump into the hit-rate dashboard updates from the past week?
[00:15] Ravi (Redwood SE): Sure. So, brief context: last week we enabled prefix cache for templates flagged as "session-stable" and turned on KV cache for frequently repeated completions. We captured telemetry across three buckets: dev traffic, spike tests, and 1% production mirror.
[00:30] Ravi: Top-line: prefix cache global hit rate moved from ~18% to ~31% on the 1% mirror. KV cache (per-conversation KV) shows a more modest lift — from 9% to about 14%. Those are median numbers, and there are tail differences by model and prompt length.
[01:02] Jenna: Nice, 31% is promising. Do you have per-prompt breakdowns? I remember we saw a lot of prompt variants in cart flow.
[01:10] Ravi: Yeah, we do. I'll attach the CSV but quick note: the top 20 prompts (by volume) contributed ~73% of cacheable prefixes. The long tail is noisy — many prompts have user-specific tokens which prevent caching.
[01:30] Priya (BrightCart PM): Is that because of user IDs in the prompts? We have a few templates that accidentally include email or user id placeholders.
[01:38] Carlos: we suspected that — some of our templating still injects internal IDs before the LLM call.
[01:42] Maya: That's an easy win then: remove user-specific tokens before calling Redwood; use metadata fields instead. Jenna, can your team scrub the top templates?
[01:51] Jenna: Yes, we'll do a pass. We can anonymize or replace with {{user_country}} etc. We'll target the top 20.
[01:58] Ravi: Great. A few other items from the telemetry: prefix cache effectiveness is highly correlated with prompt normalization. When we canonicalize prompts (strip dynamic bits, normalize whitespace), hit rates improve about 12-15% on the same set.
[02:20] Maya: That aligns with our recommendations. On the KV side, what's limiting the hit rate?
[02:25] Ravi: Two things. One, TTLs are very short in the current config — 30 seconds default — which was conservative to avoid staleness. Two, our eviction policy is LRU right now and the access patterns favor LFU for these workloads; many items are written once and rarely accessed again. Switching to LFU for the KV store yields higher effective hit rates in our sim.
[02:49] Carlos: What's the risk of LFU for memory pressure — do we see higher memory usage?
[02:53] Ravi: Slightly. LFU keeps frequently-used keys longer, so under memory constraints you'll evict large cold objects less often; depends on your memory headroom. We can run a memory-vs-hit-rate sweep.
[03:05] Jenna: On the TTL note: some of our prompts include product inventory that changes quickly, so we were worried about staleness. But for cart suggestion prompts, a 2-5 minute TTL might be fine.
[03:18] Ravi: Agreed — also we can scope TTL per-route. For product-availability prompts use shorter TTLs; for static recommendation templates go longer.
[03:26] Priya: Can Redwood set per-route policies easily in the console?
[03:30] Maya: Yes, in Redwood Console you can set route-level caching: prefix rules, KV TTL, eviction preferences. We'll send a short runbook on recommended defaults for ecommerce flows.
[03:40] Raman (Note: the transcript had a mislabel here) 
[03:42] [crosstalk] Carlos: Sorry, who is Raman?
[03:45] Maya: Ignore that, noise.
[03:46] Ravi: Next - cold-starts: we saw a 20% drop in observed hit rates during heavy burst windows because batches evicted KV entries between bursts. We should test pinned hot-keys or increase reserved memory during peak windows.
[04:05] Jenna: Can we set burst reservations on Dedicated? We're still evaluating dedicated vs hosted for this POC tier.
[04:12] Maya: On Dedicated you can reserve capacity and configure cache persistence across pods; on hosted we provide autoscaling and burst but less control over node allocation. For this POC you can test both modes; we have telemetry for both.
[04:24] Priya: Quick question - how do you compute "cacheable" prefix? If the model call includes tool calls or function calling fields, does that break caching?
[04:33] Ravi: Good question. We classify a request cacheable if the prompt and requested model/temperature/stop sequences are identical and there are no non-deterministic tool calls. Function-calling metadata currently toggles caching off by default because outputs can vary. We have a safe-mode where function calls are allowed if the function input is also identical.
[04:54] Carlos: For our use-case, we call an inventory function sometimes — so that's out. But our cart suggestions don't call external functions.
[04:59] Maya: So those should be fully cacheable once you normalize the template.
[05:02] Ravi: Right. Also a note on model variants: different quantization variants (8-bit vs 4-bit) can be considered interchangeable for caching only if you enable cross-variant keying — we normally namespace cache keys by model variant. If you want cross-variant hits, we can hash by logical model family instead, with caveats for output distribution differences.
[05:25] Jenna: That might help since we test both 8-bit and 4-bit in the POC. If we can share cache across variants, hit rates could improve. But we worry about regression in output quality.
[05:34] Ravi: We recommend enabling cross-variant only for non-deterministic prompts that are checked for semantic equivalence. We'll include a note in the runbook.
[05:42] Maya: Let's talk numbers we want for the next check-in. Ravi, what's a realistic target?
[05:46] Ravi: If BrightCart canonicalizes the top 20 prompts and increases KV TTL to 120s and switches to LFU for the KV store, I expect prefix hit rate to move to ~38-45% and KV hit to ~22-26% under mirrored traffic. That's optimistic but achievable.
[06:05] Priya: Those numbers would materially reduce token spend. Do you have an estimate on cost impact?
[06:10] Maya: Rough back-of-envelope: every 10% increase in cacheable tokens reduces per-request token consumption linearly for cached segments. With your current mix, 40% prefix hit could reduce token spend by ~16-20% depending on prompt lengths. We'll produce a clearer cost model after Ravi's benchmark.
[06:29] Carlos: For the benchmark, can you simulate our mix — short cart prompts vs long post-purchase flows?
[06:35] Ravi: Yes, we can parameterize the synthetic harness with your provided prompt set and traffic distribution. Please share the top 100 canonical prompts and their relative volumes.
[06:45] Jenna: We'll export that by next Tuesday.
[06:48] Maya: Great. A couple operational asks: we'll share a short doc on how to remove sensitive tokens from prompt pipeline, and an example of a normalization routine. Also, we'll include knobs for per-route TTLs.
[07:00] Priya: On the security/compliance side — is there any PII surface introduced by caching? Where is the cache stored and how is it encrypted?
[07:08] Maya: Cache entries are stored in our serving layer — for Hosted it's within our managed cache clusters, encrypted at rest and in transit. For Private or Dedicated we can configure the cache to use customer-managed Redis or local persistent store inside your VPC. We'll send SOC2 summary and a short note on KMS integration.
[07:27] Carlos: If we go Private, we'd probably keep the cache inside our VPC. Good to know it's supported.
[07:33] Ravi: Also worth noting: for highly sensitive prompts we'd recommend disabling caching per-route to avoid any accidental storage.
[07:40] Jenna: Makes sense.
[07:42] Maya: Any blockers from BrightCart's side for the plan?
[07:45] Jenna: None major. We'll clean the templates and provide the corpus. The only sticky bit is approving the pilot contract which I'm coordinating with finance.
[07:55] Maya: We'll push the pilot pricing and contract today.
[07:58] Priya: One more technical item — eviction policy testing. Ravi, can you outline how you'll report LFU vs LRU results?
[08:05] Ravi: I'll run a controlled run: same traffic pattern, same memory budget, toggle eviction policy and TTLs. I'll capture per-route hit rates, memory usage, and tail latency. Expect CSVs and a short readme.
[08:18] Maya: Perfect. We'll also include a quick dashboard link.
[08:22] Carlos: For the 10k benchmark, can you include cold-start windows and simulate bursts?
[08:26] Ravi: Yes — two scenarios: steady-state 10k over 1 hour, and bursty 10k within 10 minutes with cold cache initialization.
[08:35] Jenna: Do you support running the benchmark on our dedicated token so we won't hit production quotas?
[08:40] Maya: We'll use a POC token and isolated project; won't impact your prod quotas.
[08:44] Priya: Great.
[08:46] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps. Ravi to run benchmarks and share CSV, Maya to send docs and pricing, BrightCart to provide prompt set and traffic mix. We'll reconvene next week same time.
[08:58] Jenna: Works for me.
[09:00] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with artifacts. Bye.
